source.renameNote: The repository was renamed LinkFree -> BioDrop and is now ARCHIVED. The old API path answers 301 to https://api.github.com/repositories/405139301. Fetch under the canonical name; the codeload archive root is named BioDrop-<sha>, not LinkFree-<sha>.
source.pinnedRevisionVsTag: The pinned revision is the DIRECT CHILD of the v0.72.0 tag target. The two trees differ in exactly one blob — reviewpad.yml, a code-review bot config. No application source, manifest, lockfile, or profile data file differs, so this fixture's APPLICATION is byte-identical to the v0.72.0 release while its REF is one commit past the tag. Say 'the v0.72.0 application', not 'the v0.72.0 tag'. Full diff: evidence/ingests/react-linkfree-v0-72-0/tag-delta.json.

application.product: LinkFree — an open-source alternative to Linktree. A community directory in which each member has a public profile page listing their bio, avatar and outbound links, plus a searchable index of every profile.
application.frontend: create-react-app 5 single-page application, JavaScript (not TypeScript), react-router-dom v5, PrimeReact 6 component library
application.backend: NONE. There is no server, no database, and no session. The data layer is static JSON served from the application's own origin: 561 committed per-profile files plus a build-time-generated index. `serve -s build` is sufficient to run the whole application.
application.reactVersionNote: React 17 in an August 2022 application is deliberately one major behind React 18. That makes this fixture a two-axis migration target: CRA 5 -> a modern bundler AND React 17 -> React 18.
application.router: react-router-dom ^5.3.0 (lockfile-pinned 5.3.3) — the genuine v5 API: BrowserRouter + Switch + Route with children, not the v6 Routes/element API
application.componentLibrary: primereact ^6.5.1 (pinned 6.6.0) with primeflex, primeicons and the saga-blue theme, all imported wholesale in src/App.js
application.icons: react-icons ^4.3.1 behind a hand-written mapping layer, src/Components/Icons/GetIcons.js
application.styling: PrimeReact stylesheets plus per-component plain CSS files; no Tailwind, no CSS-in-JS, no preprocessor
application.singleUserMode: src/config/user.json carries a username field. When non-empty, App.js bypasses the router entirely and renders one profile — a self-host mode. It is EMPTY at the pinned revision, so the full multi-route surface is active.
application.sizeNote: The application source is modest (~36 KB across 35 files); most of the repository's bytes are the profile corpus and the 1.5 MB lockfile. It qualifies as substantive on being a real, released, multi-route product with an upstream E2E suite, not on source volume.

upstreamTestSuite.declaredCommand: npm run test:e2e — concurrently -k --success first "npm run cypress:run" "npm run start"
upstreamTestSuite.whyNotRun: Running it needs the Cypress binary, whose postinstall download the baseline's --ignore-scripts policy suppressed and whose host is outside this unit's consented acquisition allowlist.
upstreamTestSuite.significance: This fixture ships an UPSTREAM-AUTHORED behavioural oracle covering all four of its journeys. Most fixtures in this corpus have none, and their migration evidence must come from a Versionless-built oracle. Standing this suite up is a high-value follow-on unit and needs its own network consent.

legacyCell.declaredNote: The repository declares Node in TWO places and they DISAGREE. .github/workflows/build.yml pins actions/setup-node@v2 node-version '16' for both the build job and the e2e tests job, running `npm ci` then `npm run build`. The Dockerfile uses `FROM node:15` for both stages. There is no engines field, no packageManager field, no .nvmrc and no .tool-versions.
legacyCell.declarationFollowed: CI (Node 16), because CI is where the maintainers gated merges and because Node 15 was already end-of-life at the pinned date.
legacyCell.bundler: create-react-app 5.0.1 over webpack 5.73.0 (lockfile-pinned; exercised in this unit)
legacyCell.bundlerOrigin: CRA 5 / webpack 5 is this application's ORIGIN bundler. There is no vite, no rollup config, no esbuild, and no webpack config anywhere in the tree — the app is un-ejected and driven entirely by react-scripts. This is the portfolio's FIRST CRA 5 / webpack 5 cell.

node.reusedFrom: an already-acquired and digest-verified Node 16.20.2 darwin-arm64 runtime in this workspace's cache; no new runtime download was made
node.honestLabel: MAJOR-VERSION-FAITHFUL to the repository's own CI declaration. CI declares the major ('16') and not a minor, and 16.20.2 is the final Node 16 release. The only difference from the declared cell is the platform: darwin-arm64 here versus ubuntu-x64 in CI. This is a closer match to a declared cell than most fixtures in this corpus achieve.
node.unknownPreserved: Whether the outcomes below reproduce on ubuntu-x64 was not tested and is not claimed.

legacyCell.buildCommandExpands: npm run generate && react-scripts build, then npm's postbuild hook runs purgecss
legacyCell.buildEnv: CI=true, matching how the repository's own build.yml runs it
legacyCell.lifecycleScriptsCaveat: This suppressed cypress@8.7.0's postinstall (which downloads the Cypress binary from a non-allowlisted host) and `prepare: husky install`. The repository's own Dockerfile also uses --ignore-scripts, so this matches one of its declared invocations.
legacyCell.rationale: The repository's declared cell is honoured closely: its committed package-lock.json is used verbatim under `npm ci`, its declared build command is run unmodified so both the prebuild codegen and the postbuild purge fire naturally, and the Node major matches its CI declaration.

lockState.lockfileVersionNote: lockfileVersion 2 is the npm 7 / npm 8 hybrid format: it carries both the modern `packages` map and the legacy `dependencies` tree. Recorded exactly as found. This is the portfolio's FIRST npm-lock cell — the corpus previously carried yarn and pnpm locks only.
lockState.searchScope: the full recursive git tree at the pinned revision (653 blobs)
lockState.npmCiAcceptedNote: `npm ci` refuses to run when package.json and package-lock.json disagree about the dependency graph. Its success establishes that the committed lockfile is in sync with the manifest and that NOTHING was re-resolved against the 2026 registry.

versionSkew.note: The lockfile's own root entry records 0.70.1 while package.json says 0.72.0 — it was last regenerated two releases earlier and only the version string is stale. npm ci does not compare that field and did not object. Recorded as found; not corrected.

lockState.consequence: The dependency closure IS pinned by the repository and npm ci accepted it, so the build outcome below is a property of the pinned revision, not of the 2026 registry.

baseline.installDetail: npm 8.19.4 installed the committed lockfile's 1825 entries (1078 top-level package directories, 175 nested node_modules) in 11 seconds on Node 16.20.2, with npm ci accepting the lockfile and lifecycle scripts disabled. npm reported 9 deprecation warnings and 90 audit vulnerabilities (17 low, 20 moderate, 42 high, 11 critical) — expected for a four-year-old CRA 5 graph, not remediated, and no security finding is claimed.
baseline.buildDetail: `CI=true npm run build` exited 0 in 8 seconds, running all three declared steps to completion and emitting a complete static site of 583 files. This is a GREEN baseline: the portfolio's first CRA 5 cell builds clean on its own pinned closure.

declaredSteps.what: Read all 561 profile JSON files from public/data and wrote public/list.json (72625 bytes) carrying type, name, username, avatar and linkCount per profile.
declaredSteps.loadBearing: public/list.json is NOT committed. It exists only after this step. Any build lane that skips it produces an application whose home and search routes — the two most-tested journeys — have no data to load.

declaredSteps.what: CRA 5.0.1 / webpack 5.73.0 reported 'Compiled successfully.' and emitted build/static/js/main.93d99c04.js (367126 bytes raw, 103.86 kB gzip), a 4341-byte code-split chunk, and build/static/css/main.aa835dbe.css.
declaredSteps.lintGate: CRA 5 runs eslint inline during the build; with CI=true a warning would have failed it. None was raised.
warnings: Browserslist: caniuse-lite is outdated (from the 2022-pinned caniuse-lite; did not affect the exit status)

declaredSteps.what: Cut build/static/css/main.aa835dbe.css from 619824 to 50728 bytes, a 91.8% reduction, by discarding the PrimeReact 6 theme rules the built markup and scripts never reference.
declaredSteps.measurement: Measured by re-running the same declared pipeline split at the npm lifecycle boundary; see evidence/ingests/react-linkfree-v0-72-0/baseline-attempt.json.
declaredSteps.observedDefect: purgecss rewrites the .css and does NOT update the .css.map beside it, so the shipped build/static/css/main.aa835dbe.css.map remains 933691 bytes describing the pre-purge stylesheet. A real property of the legacy pipeline, relevant to any later artifact comparison.
declaredSteps.fragility: package.json declares @fullhuman/postcss-purgecss but never declares the `purgecss` CLI it invokes. The binary reached node_modules/.bin only because npm hoisted the transitive purgecss@3.1.3. The declared build works by hoisting accident, and a stricter package-manager layout would break it.

baseline.unknownPreserved: Whether these outcomes reproduce on the ubuntu-x64 cell CI declares was not tested and is not claimed. Whether the emitted site renders correctly is unknown: nothing was loaded in a browser and the upstream cypress suite was not run.

candidateJourneys: load the homepage and see the community directory (/ -> Home.js, GET /list.json) — upstream scenario in homepage.feature
navigate to search and filter the directory by name, including the empty-result state (/search -> Search.js, client-side filtering over list.json) — four upstream scenarios in search.feature
open a user profile by dynamic route segment and see their declared links (/:username -> User.js -> ProfilePage.js, GET /data/<username>.json) — three upstream scenarios in user.feature
request an unknown profile and get the not-found state (/:username with no matching data file -> ErrorPage.js, 'Profile not found') — upstream scenario in 404.feature
journeyShapeNote: Journeys here ARE route-driven, including a dynamic segment, so a witness unit can drive them by URL navigation rather than by UI state. There is no backend, no login and no session, so all four are exercisable against a static server alone.

runtimeEgress.buildTime: none — the declared build makes no network request
runtimeEgress.runtime: Avatar loads reach GitHub avatar/asset hosts (560 of 561 profiles; one contributor CDN). Image-only: no script, no XHR, no credential.
runtimeEgress.cascadeWarning: src/utils.js installs an onerror fallback to https://avatars.dicebear.com. Blocking the GitHub hosts alone REDIRECTS egress to a second live third-party host rather than eliminating it. A hermetic witness run must block or stub BOTH.
runtimeEgress.outboundLinks: The profile corpus declares 1666 anchor hrefs (top hosts: github, twitter, linkedin, instagram, youtube). These are never fetched at load time and no upstream scenario clicks one. 19 of them are malformed upstream — recorded, not corrected.

contentDataPosture.what: public/data holds 561 JSON profile files, each named by a real contributor's GitHub username and carrying a display name, bio, avatar and links.
contentDataPosture.handling: Versionless evidence treats the corpus as application content addressed by digest. It is counted, aggregate-digested and characterised by host histograms only; no individual username, filename, or field value appears in any evidence record, and none may be introduced by later work.
contentDataPosture.syntheticCorpusOption: generate.js is corpus-agnostic: it will build list.json from ANY set of profile JSON files, so a later unit can substitute a small synthetic corpus and exercise every journey without redistributing contributor data. Note that the upstream cypress scenarios assert on specific real profiles and would need rewriting against a synthetic corpus.
contentDataPosture.unknownPreserved: Whether contributors would intend their personal profile data to be redistributed within a migration-evidence corpus is not settled by the MIT grant and is recorded as unresolved in license.json.

knownRisks: The pinned revision is NOT the v0.72.0 tag target — it is that commit's child, differing by one CI bot config file (reviewpad.yml). The application is byte-identical to v0.72.0, but any document claiming this fixture IS the v0.72.0 tag would be wrong. Re-pinning to the tag target e527a935b9d37d8cde6db40f15c99ace4005280a is a live option the ingesting unit was not permitted to take.
The repository declares two conflicting Node versions (CI says 16, the Dockerfile says 15). The baseline followed CI. Anything relying on the Dockerfile's cell is untested here.

The declared postbuild step invokes a `purgecss` CLI that package.json never declares; it works only because npm hoists the transitive purgecss@3.1.3. A package-manager or layout change breaks `npm run build` with no application change.

purgecss leaves a stale CSS source map: a 933691-byte .css.map describing a stylesheet that is now 50728 bytes. Relevant to any artifact-level comparison between the legacy build and a replacement build.
public/list.json is generated, not committed. Skipping the generate.js step yields an application whose home and search journeys have no data.
The upstream cypress suite — this fixture's strongest asset — was NOT run. The Cypress binary was never downloaded, so nothing establishes that the suite passes at this revision.
The 561 profile files are real contributors' personal data. Handling rules are fixed above and must be preserved by later work.
Blocking GitHub avatar hosts without also handling avatars.dicebear.com leaves the fixture non-hermetic via the onerror fallback.
The closure carries 90 npm-audit vulnerabilities (11 critical) as a four-year-old CRA 5 graph. Recorded as an age observation; no exploitability assessment was made.

The upstream repository was renamed (LinkFree -> BioDrop) and archived. Archival is favourable — refs cannot move again — but every later fetch must use the canonical name and expect the BioDrop- archive root.
React 17 with react-router-dom v5 means a migration off this cell is a multi-axis move (bundler, React major, and router major), not a bundler swap alone.
